description: Add anonymous PostHog telemetry for first-party plugin tool usage. Emit a 'plugin_tool_used' event from the MCP server's tool dispatch pipeline, filtered to first-party npm-installed plugins (published under the '@opentabs-dev/opentabs-plugin-' scope). Exclude locally developed plugins (source='local') and sensitive-category plugins ('onlyfans', 'tinder'). After all stories pass, the server captures plugin_name, plugin_version, tool_name, success, error_category, duration_bucket, and session_id for first-party plugin tool invocations — giving the team visibility into which plugins need more engineering attention.

userStories.title: Add plugin usage telemetry predicate and capture function
userStories.description: In platform/mcp-server/src/telemetry.ts, add a first-party plugin filter (isTrackablePlugin), a duration bucketer (computeDurationBucket), and a capture function (trackPluginToolUsage) that fires a 'plugin_tool_used' PostHog event only for first-party npm-installed plugins, excluding 'onlyfans' and 'tinder'.
acceptanceCriteria: telemetry.ts exports isTrackablePlugin(plugin: RegisteredPlugin): boolean
telemetry.ts exports trackPluginToolUsage(plugin, toolName, outcome): void
isTrackablePlugin returns true only when plugin.source === 'npm' AND plugin.npmPackageName starts with '@opentabs-dev/opentabs-plugin-' AND plugin.name is not in EXCLUDED_PLUGIN_NAMES
EXCLUDED_PLUGIN_NAMES is a ReadonlySet<string> containing exactly 'onlyfans' and 'tinder'
FIRST_PARTY_NPM_SCOPE constant equals '@opentabs-dev/opentabs-plugin-'
computeDurationBucket returns '<100ms' | '<1s' | '<5s' | '>=5s' with boundaries at 100, 1000, 5000 ms (100 → '<1s', 1000 → '<5s', 5000 → '>=5s')
trackPluginToolUsage returns early (no event) when isTrackablePlugin returns false
trackPluginToolUsage calls trackEvent('plugin_tool_used', props) when the predicate passes
Event properties include session_id, plugin_name, plugin_version, tool_name, success, error_category, duration_bucket — and nothing else
error_category is 'none' when outcome.success is true, outcome.errorCategory when present, 'unknown' otherwise
No raw tab IDs, URLs, args, or error messages appear in event properties

userStories.title: Add unit tests for plugin usage telemetry
userStories.description: In platform/mcp-server/src/telemetry.test.ts, add unit tests for isTrackablePlugin (5 cases: first-party accepted; local rejected; third-party scope rejected; unscoped npm rejected; excluded names rejected) and trackPluginToolUsage (2 cases: fires event with correct properties for trackable plugin; fires nothing for untrackable plugin). Plus boundary tests for computeDurationBucket.
acceptanceCriteria: New test file section covers isTrackablePlugin with at least 5 cases
Test verifies first-party npm plugin (source='npm', npmPackageName='@opentabs-dev/opentabs-plugin-slack', name='slack') returns true
Test verifies local plugin (source='local') returns false
Test verifies third-party scope (npmPackageName='@someone/opentabs-plugin-foo') returns false
Test verifies unscoped npm (npmPackageName='opentabs-plugin-foo') returns false
Test verifies excluded name 'onlyfans' with full first-party metadata returns false
Test verifies excluded name 'tinder' with full first-party metadata returns false
trackPluginToolUsage test verifies mockCapture is called with event name 'plugin_tool_used' for trackable plugin
trackPluginToolUsage test verifies mockCapture is NOT called for an excluded plugin
All existing tests in telemetry.test.ts continue to pass

userStories.title: Emit plugin_tool_used event from dispatch pipeline
userStories.description: In platform/mcp-server/src/mcp-tool-dispatch.ts, call trackPluginToolUsage(plugin, toolBaseName, { success, errorCategory, durationMs }) inside the existing finally block of handlePluginToolCall, immediately after appendAuditEntry. Plugin is looked up from state.registry.plugins. Error category comes from errorInfo?.category. This is the final story in the PRD and must be marked as an E2E checkpoint.
acceptanceCriteria: mcp-tool-dispatch.ts imports trackPluginToolUsage from './telemetry.js' alongside the existing getSessionId/trackEvent imports

Inside handlePluginToolCall's finally block, after the existing appendAuditEntry call, a new block looks up the plugin via state.registry.plugins.get(pluginName) and calls trackPluginToolUsage when the plugin is found
trackPluginToolUsage is called with (plugin, toolBaseName, { success, errorCategory: errorInfo?.category, durationMs })
No other existing behavior in handlePluginToolCall changes — sendInvocationEnd, appendAuditEntry, activeDispatches cleanup remain exactly as before
No other call sites of trackPluginToolUsage exist in the codebase
handlePluginToolCall does not catch errors from trackPluginToolUsage (trackEvent already swallows them internally)
